sources.title: Repository tagged daily new/old login-user SQL question

claims.text: The preserved source asks for daily new and old user counts from login logs and points to left join or NOT EXISTS; concrete schema and operational boundaries are unstated.
Under the explicit user-day/lifecycle-first-login contract, the exact first-date and NOT EXISTS SQL variants produce the same new/old classification.
Same-day duplicate login events count once and new_users + old_users equals distinct active users for every validated day.

validation.command: execute both exact candidate SQL variants on independent in-memory SQLite boundary and randomized datasets against a Python reference classifier
validation.reported_stdout: PASS boundary_cases=3 randomized_datasets=600 min-date=not-exists-equivalent user-day-dedup=pass active-invariant=pass
checks: same-day duplicate events deduplicate to one user-day
first appearance is new and later appearance is old
MIN(first_date) and NOT EXISTS variants agree
new+old equals distinct active users each day

boundary_tests.case: same user logs twice on first day and returns next day
boundary_tests.expected: same-day duplicate counts once; next day is old

boundary_tests.case: mixed first-time and returning users across three dates
boundary_tests.expected: new/old partition equals distinct active users
MIN(first_date) and NOT EXISTS match reference classifier and active-user invariant

findings: The candidate preserves the sparse source boundary and explicitly declares its schema, user-day deduplication and lifecycle-first-login assumptions instead of inventing them as source facts.
Both SQL variants directly answer daily new/old user counts; the NOT EXISTS variant reflects the source hint while the first-date variant exposes the state model clearly.
The answer correctly separates event rows from distinct users so repeated logins on one day do not inflate user counts.
The lifecycle-first-date definition makes new and old mutually exclusive and exhaustive over each day’s distinct active users; independent validation checks that invariant.
Timezone, anonymous-user, history-availability, late-data and large-table access-path boundaries are explicitly called out rather than hidden.
Independent reviewer-owned SQLite execution checks three boundary families and 600 randomized datasets against a separate reference classifier; no semantic mismatch was found.
